title: Introduction to finclean package
text: finclean R package helps clean diagnose messy financial data. Real-world financial datasets often inconsistent formats, missing values, suspicious entries need addressed analysis. vignette walks function using built-sample dataset.

title: Introduction to finclean package
text: finclean comes built-sample dataset finclean_sample contains common data quality issues found financial data — messy currency strings, inconsistent fiscal year formats, account name variations, outliers, missing values.
code: data(finclean_sample) finclean_sample #>     period       account      amount revenue expenses #> 1     FY23          Rev.   $1,234.56     100       50 #> 2  Q1 2023       REVENUE        €500     200       80 #> 3  2023-Q2      Expenses     (1,200)     150      200 #> 4   Q1FY23           EXP    -$300.00   10000       60 #> 5   FY2023      Net Inc.     $98,000     130       90 #> 6  Q3-2023          COGS      $1,500     170       50 #> 7     2024 cost of goods      $2,000     160       75 #> 8     FY24        assets $99,999,999     140       65 #> 9  Q2 2024          CASH    (750.00)      NA       85 #> 10  Q4FY24        Equity      $3,200     120       55

title: Introduction to finclean package
text: Financial data often contains currency values stored strings symbols, commas, parentheses. parse_currency() converts clean numeric values. Parentheses-style negatives like "(1,200)" correctly converted -1200.

title: Introduction to finclean package
text: Fiscal year labels often inconsistent across teams systems. standardize_fiscal_year() normalizes formats consistent FY#### FY####-Q# output.
code: standardize_fiscal_year(finclean_sample$period) #>  [1] "FY2023"    "FY2023-Q1" "FY2023-Q2" "FY2023-Q1" "FY2023"    "FY2023-Q3" #>  [7] "FY2024"    "FY2024"    "FY2024-Q2" "FY2024-Q4"

title: Introduction to finclean package
text: Account names frequently abbreviated capitalized differently different people. normalize_accounts() maps variations single standardized label. Note supply custom_map, completely replace built-mapping.
code: normalize_accounts(finclean_sample$account) #>  [1] "Revenue"    "Revenue"    "Expenses"   "Expenses"   "Net Income" #>  [6] "COGS"       "COGS"       "Assets"     "Cash"       "Equity"

title: Introduction to finclean package
text: flag_outliers() detects suspicious values numeric column using either IQR method (default) z-score method. returns data frame value labeled outlier .
code: flag_outliers(finclean_sample$revenue) #>    value is_outlier #> 1    100      FALSE #> 2    200      FALSE #> 3    150      FALSE #> 4  10000       TRUE #> 5    130      FALSE #> 6    170      FALSE #> 7    160      FALSE #> 8    140      FALSE #> 9     NA         NA #> 10   120      FALSE

title: Introduction to finclean package
text: Instead checking column individually, audit_report() scans entire data frame returns structured summary missing values, duplicate counts, outliers every column.
code: audit_report(finclean_sample) #>     column      type n_missing pct_missing n_duplicates n_outliers #> 1   period character         0           0            0         NA #> 2  account character         0           0            0         NA #> 3   amount character         0           0            0         NA #> 4  revenue   numeric         1          10            0          1 #> 5 expenses   numeric         0           0            1          1

title: Introduction to finclean package
text: plot_outliers() generates bar chart highlights outlier observations red, making easy spot anomalies glance.
code: plot_outliers(finclean_sample, column = "revenue") #> Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_bar()`).

title: Financial Data Cleaning and Diagnostics Toolkit
text: finclean R package designed help analysts data scientists clean diagnose messy, inconsistent data commonly found real-world financial datasets. provides set simple powerful functions parsing currency strings, standardizing fiscal year formats, normalizing account names, detecting outliers, auditing data quality, visualizing anomalies — one place.

title: Financial Data Cleaning and Diagnostics Toolkit
text: can install finclean directly GitHub:
code: devtools::install_github("ADC-405-S26/finclean")

title: Financial Data Cleaning and Diagnostics Toolkit
text: Parse messy currency strings Standardize fiscal year formats Normalize account name variations Flag outliers using IQR method Generate full data quality audit report Visualize outliers column
code: library(finclean)  # Load the built-in sample dataset data(finclean_sample) parse_currency(c("$1,234.56", "EUR500", "(1,200)", "-$300.00")) #> [1]  1234.56   500.00 -1200.00  -300.00 standardize_fiscal_year(c("FY23", "Q1 2023", "2023-Q2", "Q1FY23")) #> [1] "FY2023"    "FY2023-Q1" "FY2023-Q2" "FY2023-Q1" normalize_accounts(c("Rev.", "REVENUE", "Expenses", "EXP", "Net Inc.")) #> [1] "Revenue"  "Revenue"  "Expenses" "Expenses" "Net Income" flag_outliers(c(100, 200, 150, 10000, 130, 170)) #>   value is_outlier #> 1   100      FALSE #> 2   200      FALSE #> 3   150      FALSE #> 4 10000       TRUE #> 5   130      FALSE #> 6   170      FALSE audit_report(finclean_sample) #>     column      type n_missing pct_missing n_duplicates n_outliers #> 1   period character         0           0            0         NA #> 2  account character         0           0            0         NA #> 3   amount character         0           0            0         NA #> 4  revenue   numeric         1          10            0          1 #> 5 expenses   numeric         0           0            2          1 plot_outliers(finclean_sample, column = "revenue")

what: Generate a Data Quality Audit Report — audit_report
title: Generate a Data Quality Audit Report — audit_report
text: Scans data frame returns summary data quality issues commonly found financial datasets. column, report includes number missing values, duplicates, numeric columns, number outliers detected using IQR method.

title: Generate a Data Quality Audit Report — audit_report
code: audit_report(df, outlier_method = "iqr", threshold = NULL)

title: Generate a Data Quality Audit Report — audit_report
text: df data frame audit. Must least one column. outlier_method single character string specifying outlier detection method use. Either "iqr" (default) "zscore". Passed flag_outliers(). threshold single numeric value controlling outlier sensitivity. "iqr", IQR multiplier (default 1.5). "zscore", z-score cutoff (default 3).

title: Generate a Data Quality Audit Report — audit_report
text: data frame one row per column df following columns: column column name. type data type column. n_missing Number NA values. pct_missing Percentage values NA. n_duplicates Number values appear , counted pairs. example, "" appears twice, counts 1 duplicate pair. n_outliers Number outliers detected. NA non-numeric columns.

title: Generate a Data Quality Audit Report — audit_report
code: df <- data.frame(   revenue = c(100, 200, 150, 10000, NA, 130),   category = c("A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C"),   expenses = c(50, 80, 70, 60, 90, 50) ) audit_report(df) #>     column      type n_missing pct_missing n_duplicates n_outliers #> 1  revenue   numeric         1        16.7            0          1 #> 2 category character         0         0.0            3         NA #> 3 expenses   numeric         0         0.0            1          0 audit_report(df, outlier_method = "zscore", threshold = 2) #>     column      type n_missing pct_missing n_duplicates n_outliers #> 1  revenue   numeric         1        16.7            0          0 #> 2 category character         0         0.0            3         NA #> 3 expenses   numeric         0         0.0            1          0

title: Sample Messy Financial Dataset — finclean_sample
text: small dataset containing common data quality issues found real-world financial data. Includes inconsistent fiscal year formats, account name variations, messy currency strings, numeric values outliers, missing values. Designed demonstrate functions finclean package.

title: Sample Messy Financial Dataset — finclean_sample
code: finclean_sample

title: Sample Messy Financial Dataset — finclean_sample
text: data frame 10 rows 5 columns: period Character. Fiscal year/quarter strings various formats e.g. "FY23", "Q1 2023", "2023-Q2". account Character. Account name strings inconsistent capitalization abbreviations e.g. "Rev.", "REVENUE". amount Character. Currency strings various messy formats e.g. "$1,234.56", "(1,200)", "-$300.00". revenue Numeric. Revenue values including extreme outlier missing value. expenses Numeric. Expense values missing entries.

title: Sample Messy Financial Dataset — finclean_sample
code: data(finclean_sample) head(finclean_sample) #>    period  account    amount revenue expenses #> 1    FY23     Rev. $1,234.56     100       50 #> 2 Q1 2023  REVENUE      €500     200       80 #> 3 2023-Q2 Expenses   (1,200)     150      200 #> 4  Q1FY23      EXP  -$300.00   10000       60 #> 5  FY2023 Net Inc.   $98,000     130       90 #> 6 Q3-2023     COGS    $1,500     170       50  # Parse the messy currency column parse_currency(finclean_sample$amount) #>  [1]     1234.56      500.00    -1200.00     -300.00    98000.00     1500.00 #>  [7]     2000.00 99999999.00     -750.00     3200.00  # Standardize the fiscal year column standardize_fiscal_year(finclean_sample$period) #>  [1] "FY2023"    "FY2023-Q1" "FY2023-Q2" "FY2023-Q1" "FY2023"    "FY2023-Q3" #>  [7] "FY2024"    "FY2024"    "FY2024-Q2" "FY2024-Q4"  # Normalize the account name column normalize_accounts(finclean_sample$account) #>  [1] "Revenue"    "Revenue"    "Expenses"   "Expenses"   "Net Income" #>  [6] "COGS"       "COGS"       "Assets"     "Cash"       "Equity"      # Flag outliers in the revenue column flag_outliers(finclean_sample$revenue) #>    value is_outlier #> 1    100      FALSE #> 2    200      FALSE #> 3    150      FALSE #> 4  10000       TRUE #> 5    130      FALSE #> 6    170      FALSE #> 7    160      FALSE #> 8    140      FALSE #> 9     NA         NA #> 10   120      FALSE  # Run a full audit on the dataset audit_report(finclean_sample) #>     column      type n_missing pct_missing n_duplicates n_outliers #> 1   period character         0           0            0         NA #> 2  account character         0           0            0         NA #> 3   amount character         0           0            0         NA #> 4  revenue   numeric         1          10            0          1 #> 5 expenses   numeric         0           0            1          1

what: Flag Outliers in a Numeric Column — flag_outliers
title: Flag Outliers in a Numeric Column — flag_outliers
text: Identifies flags suspicious values numeric vector using either IQR (interquartile range) method z-score method. Returns data frame original values logical column indicating whether value outlier.

title: Flag Outliers in a Numeric Column — flag_outliers
code: flag_outliers(x, method = "iqr", threshold = NULL)

title: Flag Outliers in a Numeric Column — flag_outliers
text: x numeric vector check outliers. method single character string specifying detection method. Either "iqr" (default) "zscore". threshold single numeric value controlling outlier sensitivity. Must greater zero. "iqr", multiplier applied IQR (default 1.5). "zscore", z-score cutoff (default 3).

title: Flag Outliers in a Numeric Column — flag_outliers
text: data frame two columns: value original numeric values x. is_outlier Logical. TRUE value flagged outlier. Returns FALSE values non-missing values identical.

title: Flag Outliers in a Numeric Column — flag_outliers
code: flag_outliers(c(100, 200, 150, 10000, 130, 170)) #>   value is_outlier #> 1   100      FALSE #> 2   200      FALSE #> 3   150      FALSE #> 4 10000       TRUE #> 5   130      FALSE #> 6   170      FALSE flag_outliers(c(100, 200, 150, 10000, 130, 170), method = "zscore") #>   value is_outlier #> 1   100      FALSE #> 2   200      FALSE #> 3   150      FALSE #> 4 10000      FALSE #> 5   130      FALSE #> 6   170      FALSE flag_outliers(c(100, 200, 150, 10000, 130, 170), method = "iqr", threshold = 3) #>   value is_outlier #> 1   100      FALSE #> 2   200      FALSE #> 3   150      FALSE #> 4 10000       TRUE #> 5   130      FALSE #> 6   170      FALSE

title: Normalize Account Name Variations — normalize_accounts
text: Standardizes inconsistent account name strings commonly found financial data single consistent label. example, variations like "Rev.", "REVENUE", "revenue" mapped "Revenue". Users can also supply custom mapping.

title: Normalize Account Name Variations — normalize_accounts
code: normalize_accounts(x, custom_map = NULL, na_on_fail = TRUE)

title: Normalize Account Name Variations — normalize_accounts
text: x character vector account name strings normalize. custom_map named character vector names desired standardized labels values regex patterns match . NULL (default), built-mapping common financial account names used. Note: providing custom_map completely replaces default mapping, built-account names longer recognized unless explicitly included custom map. na_on_fail Logical. TRUE (default), unmatched values returned NA warning. FALSE, unmatched values returned -unchanged.

title: Normalize Account Name Variations — normalize_accounts
text: character vector length x account name variations replaced standardized labels. Unmatched values returned NA unchanged depending na_on_fail.

title: Normalize Account Name Variations — normalize_accounts
code: normalize_accounts(c("Rev.", "REVENUE", "revenue", "Expenses", "EXP")) #> [1] "Revenue"  "Revenue"  "Revenue"  "Expenses" "Expenses" normalize_accounts(c("COGS", "cost of goods", "Net Inc.", "NET INCOME")) #> [1] "COGS"       "COGS"       "Net Income" "Net Income"

what: Parse Currency Strings to Numeric — parse_currency
title: Parse Currency Strings to Numeric — parse_currency
text: Converts messy currency strings commonly found financial data clean numeric values. Handles currency symbols, commas, spaces, accounting-style negative numbers written parentheses.

title: Parse Currency Strings to Numeric — parse_currency
code: parse_currency(x, na_on_fail = TRUE)

title: Parse Currency Strings to Numeric — parse_currency
text: x character vector currency strings convert. Examples supported formats: "$1,234.56", "EUR500", "(1,200)", "-$300.00","-EUR500", "1 000.50". na_on_fail Logical. TRUE (default), values parsed returned NA warning. FALSE, function stop error unparseable input.

title: Parse Currency Strings to Numeric — parse_currency
text: numeric vector length x, currency formatting removed. Parentheses-style negatives like "(500)" minus-sign negatives like "-EUR500" correctly converted -500.

title: Parse Currency Strings to Numeric — parse_currency

what: Plot Outliers in a Numeric Column — plot_outliers
title: Plot Outliers in a Numeric Column — plot_outliers
text: Generates ggplot2 bar chart numeric column data frame, highlighting flagged outlier bars red. Outliers detected using flag_outliers() colored differently easy visual identification.

title: Plot Outliers in a Numeric Column — plot_outliers
code: plot_outliers(df, column, method = "iqr", threshold = NULL, title = NULL)

title: Plot Outliers in a Numeric Column — plot_outliers
text: df data frame containing column plot. column single character string specifying name numeric column df visualize. method single character string specifying outlier detection method. Either "iqr" (default) "zscore". threshold single numeric value controlling outlier sensitivity. "iqr", IQR multiplier (default 1.5). "zscore", z-score cutoff (default 3). title single character string plot title. Defaults "Outlier Detection: <column>".

title: Plot Outliers in a Numeric Column — plot_outliers
text: ggplot2 object displaying bar chart specified column outlier bars highlighted red normal bars steelblue.

title: Plot Outliers in a Numeric Column — plot_outliers
code: df <- data.frame(revenue = c(100, 200, 150, 10000, 130, 170, 160, 140)) plot_outliers(df, column = "revenue")  plot_outliers(df, column = "revenue", method = "zscore", threshold = 2)

title: Standardize Fiscal Year Strings — standardize_fiscal_year
text: Converts variety fiscal year quarter string formats commonly found financial data single consistent format. default output format "FY2023" annual periods "FY2023-Q1" quarterly periods.

title: Standardize Fiscal Year Strings — standardize_fiscal_year
code: standardize_fiscal_year(x, prefix = "FY")

title: Standardize Fiscal Year Strings — standardize_fiscal_year
text: x character vector fiscal year strings standardize. Supported input formats include: "FY23", "FY2023", "2023", "Q1 2023", "2023-Q1", "Q1-2023", "Q1FY23". Quarter year may separated single space dash. prefix single character string use fiscal year prefix. Defaults "FY".

title: Standardize Fiscal Year Strings — standardize_fiscal_year
text: character vector length x fiscal year strings converted consistent format. Unrecognized formats returned NA warning.exact 2-digit 4-digit years accepted; 3-digit 5-digit years treated unrecognized.

title: Standardize Fiscal Year Strings — standardize_fiscal_year
